obligation: CIRCIA (Cyber Incident Reporting for Critical Infrastructure Act of 2022)
basis: No final rule. As proposed, the company would be covered under 226.2(a), because it has 850 employees against the 800-employee SBA standard for NAICS 335311 (13 CFR 121.201), and under 226.2(b)(3)(iii), because it manufactures electrical equipment (NAICS subsector 335). Tracked for readiness

obligation: ICTS connected vehicles rule
basis: The company makes transformers, TMUs and a monitoring service; no connected vehicles or vehicle systems

obligation: Export Administration Regulations (recordkeeping and screening)
basis: The company exports EAR99 transformers to utilities in the Caribbean and Central America. Export records must be kept 5 years (762.6(a)); orders are screened against restricted-party lists before release

obligation: DFARS 252.204-7012 and CMMC
basis: No DoD contracts or subcontracts; the three federal contracts are civilian and contain no DFARS clauses; the bid review gate stops any bid that would flow the clause down

obligation: NERC CIP-013-2 Supply Chain Risk Management (direct obligation)
basis: Applies to the Responsible Entities in section 4.1; the company is not a NERC-registered entity. Its duties arrive only through the utility addenda (CON-ADDENDA)

obligation: NERC CIP-013-3
basis: Subject to future enforcement; tracked because utilities are expected to revise their addenda before it takes effect

obligation: Utility Supplier Cyber Security Addenda (31 utilities)
citation: Utility addendum secs. 1-6 (CIP-013-2 R1 Part 1.2 flow-down)
basis: 31 purchase agreements require incident notice within 48 hours (22 utilities) or 24 hours (9 utilities), access-revocation notice within 1 business day, vulnerability disclosure within 30 days, hashes or signatures, and utility-controlled MFA remote access

obligation: Basic Safeguarding of Covered Contractor Information Systems
basis: The clause is in all three federal contracts, and FCI (specifications, drawings, delivery schedules, test reports) resides in company systems (FAR 4.1903)

obligation: Kaspersky covered articles
basis: In each federal contract's clause list; reports within 3 business days, then 10 business days

obligation: Covered telecommunications and video surveillance equipment
basis: In each federal contract; (b)(2) covers use of covered equipment regardless of contract; report within 1 business day of identification, then 10 business days

obligation: FASCSA orders
basis: In each federal contract's clause list; SAM.gov review at least once every three months ((c)(1)); reports within 3 business days, then 10 business days

obligation: FAR overhaul numbering (FAR 52.240-93 and 52.240-91 under agency FAR Part 40 class deviations)
basis: The three awarded contracts keep FAR 52.204-21, -23 and -25 until modified; new awards under a deviation would carry the new numbers with the same requirements

obligation: FMS subscription agreements
basis: 99.5% monthly portal availability with service credits, status page update within 1 hour of an outage, incident notice within 72 hours, and confidentiality of utility data

obligation: Subscriber requirement for a SOC 2 Type 2 report on the FMS
basis: The two largest subscribers require a SOC 2 Type 2 report (Security, Availability, Confidentiality) before their renewals on 2027-12-31

obligation: Florida Information Protection Act (breach notification)
basis: The company holds personal information of employees and applicants in Florida, and the HR, payroll and applicant tracking vendor is a third-party agent

obligation: Breach notification laws of other states
citation: The law of each state where affected individuals reside
basis: Applies when a breach affects employees or applicants who live outside Florida

obligation: NIST CSF 2.0 with NIST SP 800-82 Rev. 3 (OT benchmark)
basis: No binding sector-wide cyber rule applies; the company uses CSF 2.0 with SP 800-82 Rev. 3 as its yardstick for IT, both plants, its products and the FMS

obligation: SEC cybersecurity incident and governance disclosure rules
basis: The company is privately held

obligation: HIPAA Privacy, Security and Breach Notification Rules
basis: The company is not a covered entity or business associate, and the employee health plan is fully insured

obligation: Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard
basis: Customers pay by bank transfer; no payment cards are accepted
